name: Tennessee
summary: A red field with a blue disc edged in white containing three white stars, and a narrow blue vertical bar at the fly. Designed by Colonel LeRoy Reeves of the 3rd Tennessee Infantry.
origin: LeRoy Reeves, an officer in the Tennessee National Guard, designed the flag; it was adopted on 17 April 1905.

symbols.name: Three stars
symbols.description: White stars in a blue disc.
symbols.meaning: The three Grand Divisions of Tennessee: East, Middle and West, bound together by the circle.

symbols.name: Blue bar
symbols.description: A narrow vertical bar at the fly.
symbols.meaning: Reeves explained it as a finishing touch so the flag would not look too red when hanging limp.

facts: The three Grand Divisions are legally recognised regions of the state.
The blue bar was added so the flag would look less like a plain red flag when hanging.
It ranks among the better-designed US state flags in surveys.
clues: Red with a blue disc containing three white stars and a narrow blue bar at the fly.
Its three stars stand for three Grand Divisions.
Its fly bar was added so it would not look too red when limp.
